metadata.summary: Pep Guardiola has posted a message of support to Manchester City's players, staff, fans and ownership saying: "We will get through this together. I love you all."
metadata.content: Man City Premier League charges: Pep Guardiola sends message of support to former club | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Man City Premier League charges: Pep Guardiola sends message of support to former club Man City have been found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission; City were charged by the Premier League with more than 100 breaches in February 2023; City continue to deny the breaches and intend to appeal decision Wednesday 30 September 2026 13:44, UK Image: Pep Guardiola with the Premier League trophy after winning the title in the 2017/18 season Pep Guardiola has posted a message of support to Manchester City's players, staff, fans and ownership saying: "We will get through this together. I love you all." Man City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission. The independent commission found that between 2009/10 and 2017/18, Manchester City arranged "sham" contracts with a number of its commercial partners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £830m. The club continue to deny the breaches, with chief executive Ferran Soriano calling the process a "Premier League conspiracy theory" in a video message to players and staff . messages.text: Could Willis switch allegiance from England to Ireland?

metadata.summary: Jack Willis hinted he could be open to switching allegiances to play for Ireland, as the flanker remains ineligible for England selection.
metadata.content: England flanker Jack Willis opens door to switching allegiance to Ireland | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England flanker Jack Willis opens door to switching allegiance to Ireland Toulouse flanker Jack Willis remains ineligible for England selection under the RFU’s restrictions on overseas-based players, but the back rower could qualify to represent Ireland and has hinted he would be open to playing for Andy Farrell’s side Wednesday 30 September 2026 09:38, UK Image: Jack Willis won the last of his 14 England caps at the 2023 Rugby World Cup Jack Willis hinted he could be open to switching allegiances to play for Ireland, as the flanker remains ineligible for England selection. The 29-year-old Toulouse back row has enjoyed another standout season in the Top 14, being crowned the league's Player of the Season for the second year running this week. The Rugby Football Union (RFU) currently restricts overseas-based players from representing England, meaning Willis has been unable to add to his 14 international caps since the 2023 Rugby World Cup. He won his last cap during England's group-stage victory over Chile and remains under contract with Toulouse until 2029.
